title: Customer Assurance Portal Handler and Evidence Assembly Orchestrator
creator: Ana Rodriguez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of assurance requests (SOC2 scoping, ISO docs, HIPAA dataflow questions, GDPR/DPA clauses, and long vendor questionnaires). Our current intake relies on email/Forms and manual routing to Security or Solutions, causing SLA misses, duplicated work, and slow evidence turnaround.

Goal: Build a lightweight orchestration layer — the Assurance Portal Handler — that classifies incoming security/compliance requests, assigns a priority lane (auto/SLA/manual), assembles a preliminary evidence package from canonical sources, and issues an immediate first-response with expected SLAs. The Evidence Assembly Orchestrator is responsible for fetching proof artifacts (SOC2 cert, dataflow diagrams, KMS scope, contract templates), redacting sensitive bits, and producing a shareable bundle.

Scope (MVP):
- Public-facing webhook + portal endpoint for intake (no auth for initial MVP via signed link)
- Automatic classifier to tag requests into taxonomy: SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA/vendor-questionnaire/other
- Decision graph to map taxonomy + customer tier + region to a lane: auto-response, 48h SLA, 7d SLA, or manual review escalation
- Evidence bundler that pulls artifacts from Drive/Confluence/S3 and returns a zipped bundle with provenance metadata
- Async autoresponder that provides an evidence bundle preview + next steps and SLA expectations
- Telemetry: time-to-first-response, bundle completeness %, manual-escalation-rate, and customer satisfaction seed survey

Out of scope (MVP):
- Full SSO gated portal for customers (we will integrate SSO on Dedicated iteration)
- Deep questionnaire parsing and auto-answers beyond metadata extraction (future work)
acceptance_criteria: Portal accepts intake via webhook and the web form; classifier tags requests with >=85% accuracy on taxonomy sample
Decision graph assigns lane correctly for 95% of test permutations (customer_tier x request_type x region)
Evidence bundler returns a bundle with at least one canonical artifact for each request type 90% of the time
Autoresponder is sent within 15 minutes of intake for auto-lane; 48h SLA lane gets acknowledgement within 4 hours
End-to-end telemetry is surfaced in Console with per-request trace and SLA status

notes: Design trade-offs: We prefer early automation that reduces manual touch but we must cap blast radius — auto-lane should never supply contractual commitments without human sign-off.
Risk: Over-automation may surface inaccurate evidence. Mitigation: provenance metadata + human-in-loop approval for P0 customers and contractual artifacts.
Privacy: Bundler will redact token-like strings and customer PII. Security team requires an audit trail for each extraction and redaction action.
Operational runbook: If bundler fails to assemble >50% of required artifacts, route to Solutions queue and flag as 'evidence-missing' with suggested owner list.
